title: Late Breaking Results: Language-level QoR modeling for High-Level Synthesis
problem: Predicting the quality-of-results (performance and resource requirements) of High-Level Synthesis applications when different synthesis directives (pragmas) are applied to source code.
motivation: Accurate QoR prediction enables efficient design space exploration and optimization of HLS applications without the cost of running full synthesis iterations.
method: A Transformer-based neural network architecture that processes HLS source code directly, learning to map code representations and synthesis directives (#pragmas) to predicted performance and resource metrics. The model performs language-level analysis to understand how pragmas affect synthesis outcomes.
key_novelty: Language-level QoR modeling using Transformer architecture to predict HLS performance and resource requirements directly from source code with synthesis pragmas.
contributions: Language-level modeling approach for HLS applications operating directly on source code
Transformer-based architecture achieving 96.02% accuracy for HLS feasibility classification
Prediction of performance and resource requirements with 0.95 and 0.91 R2 scores respectively
Enables efficient design space exploration by predicting outcomes of different synthesis directives

metrics.accuracy: 96.02% feasibility classification accuracy; 0.95 R2 for performance; 0.91 R2 for resource prediction

primary_theme: transformer-based QoR prediction for high-level synthesis
